title: Power-series coordinates on the actual normalized curve branches
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $X$ a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pure-dimension], $x$ a closed point, and $
u:X^
u	o X$ its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Enumerate the distinct points of its fibre as $y_1,\ldots,y_b$, with $1\le b<\infty$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=(
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})_x$, $H=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m_A^n$, $C=\varprojlim_n B/\mathfrak m_A^n B$, and $R_i=\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_{X^
u,y_i}/\mathfrak m_{y_i}^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Each $\mathcal O_{X^
u,y_i}$ and each $R_i$ is a discrete valuation ring, meaning a local principal ideal domain which is not a field; $R_i$ is complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and its residue field is $k$ by the structural map. There is a canonical $H$-algebra isomorphism $C\cong\prod_{i=1}^b R_i$. For every choice of generators $t_i$ of the maximal ideals of $R_i$, evaluation with the structural coefficients and $T_i\mapsto t_i$ gives a $k$-algebra isomorphism $k[[T_i]]\cong R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. These maps identify $C$ with $D=\prod_{i=1}^b k[[T_i]]$. For every $h\in H$, all constant coefficients of its images in these factors are equal to its residue in $H/\mathfrak m_H=k$. In particular the image of $H$ under the constant-coefficient map $D	o k^b$ is exactly the diagonal copy of $k$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), (8), and proof of Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion); algebra.tex Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension) and Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), clause (2). Agent refinement preserving the actual fibre indices and structural residue maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-curve-delta-completion-data] to the given $k,X,x,\nu$. It gives the finite nonempty fibre of closed points with structural residue fields $k$, the reduced Noetherian local ring $A$ of dimension one, its structural residue field $k$, and the finite integral closure $A\hookrightarrow B\subset Q(A)$. It also identifies the specified inverse-limit ring $C$ canonically with $B\otimes_A H$ and makes $H$ complete local with structural residue field $k$. Thus the displayed enumeration of distinct fibre points is legitimate and $1\le b<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), (1), (3), (6), (7); finite fibres and residue fields in Tag 0C45 (lemma-normalize-noetherian-dim-1).

proof.text: The field $k$ is excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent]. The essentially finite-type presentation of $A$ in Step 1 expresses it as a localization of a finite-type $k$-algebra, so [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] makes $A$ excellent. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] it is quasi-excellent; [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata] therefore makes $A$ Nagata. This verifies the extra hypothesis needed for the algebraic DVR-branch statement below, without assuming that reducedness alone suffices for arbitrary completions.

Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$, with point $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure], $\nu^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}T$, $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}T$, compatibly with structural maps. Points $y_i$ correspond to primes $Q_i\subset T$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], extension and contraction give exactly the primes $\mathfrak q_i\subset B$ over $\mathfrak m_A$. Indeed a prime over $\mathfrak m_A$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$ in $R$, and conversely a prime over $\mathfrak p$ is disjoint from $R\setminus\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $\mathcal O_{X^\nu,y_i}=T_{Q_i}$. Its canonical identification with $B_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is explicit: the map $T\to T_{Q_i}$ inverts $R\setminus\mathfrak p$, then every element of $B\setminus\mathfrak q_i$, giving $B_{\mathfrak q_i}\to T_{Q_i}$. Conversely $T\to B_{\mathfrak q_i}$ inverts $T\setminus Q_i$, giving the inverse. The two composites fix $T$ and its inverted elements, hence are identities. They fix $R$, so identify the local structural maps from $A$, not just abstract rings.

source.place: Tag 0C3B (lemma-stalk-normalization) and Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); algebra.tex Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nagata-normalization-dvr-branches] to the reduced local Nagata ring $A$ of dimension one and its integral closure $B$. It gives that each $B_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is a DVR, hence so is the actual local ring $\mathcal O_{X^\nu,y_i}$ of Step 3. Now [lem-trf-finite-dvr-branch-completion] applies: $A$ is Noetherian local of dimension one, $A\hookrightarrow B$ is finite and injective, and every prime over $\mathfrak m_A$ is one of the $\mathfrak q_i$. The isomorphism is induced by the completed local maps $H\to\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q_i}}$, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension]. Together with Step 1 it gives $C=B\otimes_A H\cong\prod_i\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q_i}}=\prod_i R_i$, and each $R_i$ is a DVR. The last equality is induced by the local isomorphisms in Step 3 on every maximal-ideal quotient. Thus these are exactly the specified factors, indexed by the actual points $y_i$.

source.place: Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion), last paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension); more-algebra.tex Tag 0AP1 (lemma-completion-dvr).

proof.text: Write $L_i=\mathcal O_{X^\nu,y_i}$ and $\mathfrak n_i=\mathfrak m_{y_i}$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], a DVR is equivalently a Noetherian local domain with nonzero principal maximal ideal, so $\mathfrak n_i$ is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]: the maximal ideal of $R_i$ is $\mathfrak n_iR_i$, the kernel of its first projection, and the structural completion map identifies its residue field with $L_i/\mathfrak n_i$. By Step 1 the latter is $k$ via the structural map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] to $L_i$, $I=\mathfrak n_i$, $M=L_i$. It makes $R_i$ complete for the extended ideal $\mathfrak n_iR_i$, hence for its own maximal ideal. Powers of that extended ideal equal the extended powers because both are generated by the corresponding products of generators.

For each $i$, [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] gives $\dim R_i=1$. The Noetherian characterization in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and a generator $t_i$ of its maximal ideal show from [def-weil-regular-scheme] that $R_i$ is regular local: the maximal ideal has one generator, precisely its dimension. Step 5 gives completeness and the specified coefficient map $k\to R_i$ inducing the residue isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates] with $d=1$ and this particular generator $t_i$. It gives the $k$-algebra isomorphism $e_i:k[[T_i]]\xrightarrow{\sim}R_i$ using structural coefficients and $e_i(T_i)=t_i$. Taking the product and composing its inverse with Step 4 identifies $C$ with $D=\prod_i k[[T_i]]$ as claimed. This works for every choice of the generators.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), equivalence with regular local of dimension one; Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), (2) and its proof with prescribed parameters.

proof.text: Fix $h=(h_n)_n\in H$. The $i$th structural map $H\to R_i$ is the completed local map from $A\to L_i$ in Step 4. Its first projection is the map $A/\mathfrak m_A\to L_i/\mathfrak n_i$ applied to $h_1$: this follows componentwise from [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], since $\mathfrak m_A^n$ maps into $\mathfrak n_i^n$. Both residue maps identify the structural field $k$ with the residue field, so this residue map is the identity on $k$. If $f=e_i^{-1}(h|_{R_i})$, write $f=a_0+T_i g$ by shifting its coefficient sequence [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $e_i(f)=c_i(a_0)+t_i e_i(g)$, so its residue is exactly $a_0$. Thus every constant coefficient is the residue $h_1\in k$, which is also the residue of $h$ in $H/\mathfrak m_H$ by Step 1. The image lies in the diagonal. Conversely, the structural image in $H$ of any $a\in k$ maps to the constant series $a$ in every factor because each $e_i$ is a $k$-algebra map. Every diagonal tuple therefore occurs, proving equality with the diagonal copy of $k$.

source.place: Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension), compatibility of completed local maps; Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), (2); elementary first-projection and constant-coefficient calculation.
